justification: Both round-1 blockers are fixed and verified directly against pixels, not just source diffs. (1) Both OUTPUT panels that previously printed the full SqliteException text now print only `ex.SqliteErrorCode` ('A's COMMIT: failed (code 5)', 'B's UPDATE: failed (code 5)'); checked mobile-light/dark part11 (blocked-write demo) and mobile-light/dark part16 (lock-cycle demo) -- both OUTPUT panels are now short enough to render with zero right-edge fade, fully legible in both themes, with no scrolling needed. The prose that follows still explains SQLITE_BUSY and quotes 'database is locked' in running text (mobile-light/dark part15), which is exactly the fix the round-1 review suggested (shorten what's printed, keep the explanation in prose). (2) The isolation-level table's header row was shortened to 'Level | Dirty | Non-repeat | Phantom' and every cell to Yes/No. Checked at 2x-upscaled native resolution (mobile-light/dark part06, plus a cropped/upscaled close-up of the table specifically): the Dirty, Non-repeat and Phantom column *values* (Yes/Yes/Yes/No down the Phantom column) are now all fully visible inside the initial 390px viewport in both themes, un-faded -- this is the exact information Exercise 2's solution depends on ('Repeatable Read still allows phantom reads'), and it no longer requires scrolling to check. This is a substantial improvement over round 1, where the entire fourth column -- header and all four values -- was scrolled off past the right edge with no visible content at all. A residual, much smaller cosmetic issue remains: the header word 'Phantom' itself is still one character short of fitting ('Phanto' visible, fading into 'm') because header cells are left-aligned at full column width while the short Yes/No values sit flush left within that same column and clear the fold first. This does not hide any data -- the reader has already read 'Phantom read' by name three times in the prose and the exercise directly above the table before reaching it -- so I score it a minor polish item, not a blocker. Beyond the two targeted fixes, a fresh full pass found no regressions: Figure 1 (dirty-read timeline) and Figure 2 (lock-cycle) both still render correctly in light and dark with proper accent/bad color swaps and no scrolling of the diagram canvas itself (checked mobile-light/dark parts 06, 16-17 and desktop-light part04, desktop-dark part09); heading hierarchy remains a clean flat H2 list with correctly nested TOC; all three exercises are embedded at point of use and collapse correctly ('Show solution' triangle, checked light and dark); every SQL RESULT and C# OUTPUT panel elsewhere in the article (parts 05, 08-10, 12-15) remains fully legible with no new clipping; prose/code/output rhythm is unchanged and still tight. Lighthouse is a clean 98/100/100/100 on this serial run, 0 console errors, 0 console warnings, 0 broken links, 0px mobile overflow; the only verify failure is the expected NEEDS_MARKUS owner-supplied byline placeholder. This clears the >=8.5 design bar.
